title: Professional Identity and Development
tagline: Becoming the counselor you are training to be.
welcome: Beyond techniques is the person. This course forms your professional identity: your philosophy, your ethics, your community, and your lifelong growth plan.
vignette: A new graduate is asked, 'What kind of counselor are you?' She pauses, then answers with a coherent philosophy of person, change, and ethics. That answer is the course's product.
vignette_attr: A graduation conversation, drawn from experience
description: A course in professional identity: the history and values of the counseling profession, professional organizations and credentials, a personal philosophy of counseling, wellness and burnout prevention, lifelong learning and supervision, and advocacy for the profession and for children.
questions: Who am I as a counselor, and on what ground?
How will I stay well and growing across a career?
What do I owe the profession and the public?
importance: Identity predicts resilience and ethical consistency
Professional community prevents isolation and drift
Advocacy protects children and the profession
misconceptions: that identity is fixed at graduation, when it is developed across a career
that self-care is indulgence, when it is professional duty
figures: who defined counseling as a distinct discipline
who model the identity you refine
which carry the standards and community
outcomes: You will state your view of person, change, and ethics.
Know the profession's history and values
You will locate yourself in the field's story.
You will join organizations and networks.
You will build a sustainable professional life.
You will design your growth and supervision path.
Advocate for children and the profession
You will act beyond the consulting room.
modules: Know whose shoulders you stand on.
Wellness is ethics applied to yourself.
Growth does not end at graduation.
For children and for the profession
tips: Write your philosophy now and revisit yearly
Join one professional community this term
integration: Identity integrates and sustains every competence in the degree.
faith: We form our professional selves as a calling, accountable to God and to the child.
closing: May you know who you are as a counselor, and may that knowing steady you for decades.
